Servant leadership is present but unnamed: design thinking "begin with the person you are trying to serve", systems thinking replacing "who is responsible?" with "what structure makes this failure the natural result?", and /resources serving before asking ("no contact details required", "No score or data submission is required"). The Service rung is absent from every CTA; CTAs are process labels ("Read →", "Explore the programme", "Get the free 2026 programme guide", "Send my programme request →"). summary: The English copy in this cluster is honest, exact and low-pressure (it already passes the governance bar), but it frames the offer mostly as FEATURE (what the programme has: 6 months, 6 days, 12 modules, CMI, cohorts) and SOLUTION/DECISION-SUPPORT (guide, checklist, facts to verify). CHANGE OF EXPERIENCE is present but buried: the audience points ("Bring a current business issue. / Learn through a rigorous structure that fits around work. / Leave with a practical plan you can explain, test and act on."), the experience section ("A working room built around real decisions.") and the diagnostic Q2 options are the strongest before-to-after lines on the site. The diagnostic is JTBD-shaped (why now / where would structure help) but its result is a static, feature-only checklist that does not reflect the reader's chosen state back. Naming drift undermines the "one thing" principle: the guide is called "free 2026 guide", "free 2026 programme guide", "Future Ready EMBA guide", "private decision guide", "The Working Manager's 2026 Progression Guide", "advancement brief" and, in the confirmation email, "programme plan"; the diagnostic is "Programme fit check" in NAV, "Working Manager Progression Check" in metadata and "Your private review checklist" on the result. summary:
Read in full: SEO-CONTENT-GOVERNANCE.md, content-clarity-audit.mjs (banned patterns + file scope), the ten listed files, and the content.ts constants they interpolate (CTA_LABELS, NAV, FACTS, HRD_CORP_CLAIM, PROGRAMME_POSITIONING_SENTENCE, OPERATOR, SITE, CERTIFICATE_POSITIONING). 17 copy units mapped.

FRAME FINDING. The cluster is overwhelmingly FEATURE-framed (what the programme has, what the guide contains, what the team will send) sitting on a strong, well-executed 5S SAFETY rung (no payment, not admission, confirmed in writing, PDPA, named coordinator). That Safety layer is the trust asset and must survive any rewrite. PROGRESS/HOPE appears in only three places: the decision-guide PDF cover ("Made for the decision you're facing now." / "the responsibility you already carry — not just the title you would like next."), LeadForm step 1 ("What are you planning for?") and CtaSection ("Get the facts you need to decide."). CHANGE OF EXPERIENCE is documented factually but buried: "the applied work happens inside your business between sessions" (day7), "Judgment on your own live business issue" (decision-guide table), "define a problem, weigh options and turn a decision into an action plan" (decision-guide method card). These evidence-backed activity descriptions are the only permissible raw material for experience framing, because governance bans outcome framing (promotion, board-ready, future-proof). RIGHT-VS-GOOD seeds exist: "The calendar decides more than the brochure does", "The outcome is applied, not just attendance", "Clear terms protect everyone", "not just the title you would like next", and the chatbot Comparison rule. SERVANT LEADERSHIP shows only as mechanics ("the team reads every reply", "tell the team before you rule it out", "Decide your next step after receiving the information", Roy Affandi named) — never as a stated posture. 5S: Survival n/a; Safety strong; Social absent (no cohort/peer copy in this cluster); Success present as "Career progression" intent label and PROGRAMME_AUDIENCE; SERVICE rung absent except implicitly in the employer brief — the largest untapped lever, usable only via "responsibility for people" language, never results.

GOVERNANCE BREACHES FOUND (current copy, not framework proposals): (1) nurture day3 "Most readers tell us three sections decide it for them" — banned norm "most" and an unsupported participant claim under the evidence standard; (2) nurture day7 "the calendar conversation is usually the shortest one" — banned "usually"; (3) nurture day3/day7 "3 scheduled weekends" / "3 weekend sessions" / "no time out of the business" — fact drift against chat-knowledge.ts attendance fact (only English Cohort 17 is Sat–Sun; other cohorts Fri–Sat); (4) en.json decision-guide table "Typically 18–24 months" — banned "typically", COMPARISON_SCOPE gives the exact figure; (5) en.json employer-funding-brief kicker "EMPLOYER DECISION BRIEF" matches banned "decision brief", and promise "questions a sponsor usually asks" — banned "usually"; (6) en.json working-managers-guide CTA "Request the programme guide or arrange a conversation" matches the retired CTA pattern "Request the programme guide" and is circular inside the guide; (7) llms.txt "[Apply]: the enrolment enquiry form" conflates the controlled terms enrolment/enquiry; (8) employer brief notice "authorised programme partner" departs from the controlled role "marketing agency". Borderline: "One conversation. No commitment." / "no follow-up pressure" (day14), "no-obligation" (decision guide) sit beside the banned "no-pressure enquiry" device and the banned ZH 无需承诺; "private decision guide" (LeadForm campaign helper, decision-guide kicker) sits beside banned "private decision tool" and adds a third name for the same PDF ("programme guide", "Working Manager's Guide", "programme plan"). Root cause: src/lib/nurture-email.ts and scripts/pdf/copy/*.json are NOT in content-clarity-audit.mjs's file list, so npm run audit:content never sees them — recommend adding both before any rewrite.

FRAMEWORK/GOVERNANCE COLLISION RULES for the rewrite: "sometimes the shortcut cuts" may only be expressed as a difference in purpose and documentation between routes (as COMPARISON_SCOPE and the chatbot Comparison rule already do), never as a judgement on HRD Corp providers, attendance-only training or academic MBAs; "progress" must be described as what the participant does during the six months (activities, decision processes, the applied project in their own business), never what happens to their career after; "hope" must not become urgency (no seat counts, countdowns, "remaining" beyond the factual calendar); "deserving through serving" may describe the team's posture (serve answers first, the reader decides, "no" is a valid outcome) but never the scholarship, where it would read as selection criteria; Service-rung wording may reference responsibility for people but not organisational outcomes or ROI. Every new sentence must be sourced from content.ts constants (governance: pages, emails, chatbot and llms.txt reuse facts, never independent versions).
